Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luca Fernandez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood Partner Lead) — Samir Patel (Bluehaven Head of Alliances), Talia Morgan (Dir Field Sales), Ben Ortiz (Field CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-gen):

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — I know it's a busy week so we'll try to keep this tight. quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Samir Patel: Samir here, thanks Maya. Talia and Ben on as well.
[00:00:18] Talia Morgan: hey all. good to be here.
[00:00:21] Ben Ortiz: Ben, Field CTO. ready to dig in.
[00:00:25] Luca Fernandez: Luca from Redwood, SE — I'll be focused on any technical scoping.
[00:00:29] Priya Rao: Priya, partner lead — thinking about field enablement and incentives.

[00:01:10] Maya Chen: super. quick agenda: 1) review the co-sell playbook we've been piloting, 2) triage the shared pipeline Samir sent yesterday, 3) align on next steps for enabling the field. if anything else please add.
[00:01:28] Samir Patel: sounds good. hi-level — Bluehaven's strategy is to lean partner-led for enterprise verticals: finance and healthcare. momentum in three accounts right now, and we want Redwood to be the inference partner for all of them.
[00:01:45] Talia Morgan: the crux: our reps need a simple way to route prospects to Redwood without slowing cycles. we can't add multi-week approvals for every intro.
[00:02:05] Maya Chen: totally — that's why the playbook has a lightweight intro flow and a handoff SLA (48h) for AE→SE. also an auto-assessment to flag SOC2/data residency needs.
[00:02:22] Ben Ortiz: quick interjection — for the healthcare deals we need VPC or on-prem options, and proof of pseudo-anonymization. can Redwood support a short-term scoped on-prem POC?
[00:02:40] Luca Fernandez: yes, we have a Redwood Private reference package. for a short scoped POC we can do a two-week pilot with a trimmed dataset. caveats: procurement and security review often add time — usually 3–6 weeks extra.

[00:03:12] [sound of paper rustling]
[00:03:20] Priya Rao: on incentives — Bluehaven asked about co-sell splits. we propose a 60/40 credit split for partner-led closes where Bluehaven drives the demo and first tech contact. how flexible is Redwood on that?
[00:03:37] Maya Chen: we can be flexible in pilot phase. our standard is to provide joint credits and a bonus for sourced deals > $200k. we should capture deals in the spreadsheet so ops can calculate credit.
[00:03:52] Samir Patel: good. also, how do we prevent double-counting or disputes? we need a clear lead ownership timestamp.
[00:04:05] Maya Chen: the playbook uses an email timestamp (first intro to redwood-sales@redwood.com) as canonical ownership plus a short intake form. ops will reconcile weekly.

[00:04:33] Talia Morgan: moving to the pipeline triage — Samir, you shared 14 accounts; can we walk through the top 8 quickly?
[00:04:42] Samir Patel: sure. I'll flag high-risk ones. first is Apollo Financial — in discovery; procurement is slow; no SOC2 certification yet.
[00:04:55] Maya Chen: risk note: Apollo would need a VPC deployment and SOC2 controls — likely lengthen cycle. mark as "security/procurement risk".
[00:05:12] Luca Fernandez: technical note: Apollo's expected sequence lengths are long (6–8k tokens) — recommend benchmarking with our long-context variants, maybe a quantized LLM that preserves throughput.
[00:05:29] Ben Ortiz: those long contexts add GPU cost. Bluehaven comp would need to understand unit economics.
[00:05:36] Priya Rao: yes — let's capture recommended model profile per account in the spreadsheet.

[00:06:10] [00:06:10] Samir Patel: second account is Meridian Health — compliance-heavy, wants on-prem and data residency in EU.
[00:06:20] Maya Chen: for Meridian, we should push Redwood Private+KMS integration. procurement will ask for KMS/HSM and audit logs. we have a compliance pack we can share.
[00:06:32] Talia Morgan: how long to stand up Private in a customer's VPC? some of our reps worry it's a multi-month project.
[00:06:41] Luca Fernandez: typical timeline 4–8 weeks depending on networking and approvals. we've done accelerated installs in 2–3 weeks for enterprise with a dedicated infra team. but require firewall exceptions and SAML SSO config.

[00:07:05] Maya Chen: note — we should mark Meridian as "high touch" and pair a dedicated SE for onboarding.

[00:07:22] [00:07:22] Ben Ortiz: third deal — Helix Investments. they're price-sensitive and likely to go hosted unless we can show cost parity for dedicated capacity. any ideas?
[00:07:33] Maya Chen: propose a committed Dedicated discount for 12 months plus pre-warmed pools to hit latency SLOs. also offer a caching/batching recommendation to reduce token costs.
[00:07:48] Talia Morgan: reps want a one-pager showing expected monthly spend ranges under hosted vs dedicated. can Redwood supply that?
[00:07:56] Luca Fernandez: yes — we'll produce a cost-comparison one-pager with assumptions. I'll include sample configs (batch sizes, kv cache hit rates).

[00:08:20] [background murmur]
[00:08:28] Samir Patel: fourth is CedarTech — a strategic account; they've reached out to multiple vendors including Anthropic. they want an architecture deep-dive.
[00:08:40] Maya Chen: competitor callout — CedarTech is evaluating Anthropic and VertexAI. we should highlight runtime optimizations (latency, cost/ttk) and our recent benchmark for streaming and function calls.
[00:08:58] Ben Ortiz: for CedarTech we should propose an on-site architecture workshop and provide a reference architecture doc.

[00:09:18] Luca Fernandez: quick tech piece — if CedarTech wants sub-100ms token latency at 16k context we should propose a hybrid: dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels + local cache. we'll sketch that at the workshop.

[00:09:40] Maya Chen: okay high-level triage complete — we marked accounts as: 3 high-touch, 2 compliance-heavy, 2 price-sensitive, 1 strategic competitor risk.

[00:10:02] Priya Rao: enablement — what's in the playbook for field demos? reps need a 20-minute partner-led demo script and a one-click demo environment.
[00:10:12] Maya Chen: we have a partner demo kit: slide deck, pre-recorded 10-min videos, and a quick sandbox flow. we'll add a one-click demo link in the playbook.
[00:10:25] Talia Morgan: can Bluehaven reps get access to the sandbox as "partner" role? we need RBAC to limit editing.
[00:10:34] Luca Fernandez: yes, we can provision partner-only access with restricted keys; logs are auditable.

[00:10:50] Samir Patel: procurement question — for the larger deals, do you support net-new SOWs that include customization? our services org will want a predictable SOW template.
[00:11:02] Maya Chen: Redwood supports a standard SOW template for pilots and an add-on for professional services. we'll attach a sample SOW to the shared drive.

[00:11:15] [00:11:15] Ben Ortiz: security reviewers will request SOC2 report and pen-test results. do you have an NDA-friendly bundle?
[00:11:23] Maya Chen: yes — security pack with SOC2 summary, pen-test redacted report, and KMS docs. we'll send it to Samir after the call.

[00:11:40] Priya Rao: curious: has Redwood run a co-sell incentive pilot with other partners? any lessons learned on payout timing?
[00:11:50] Maya Chen: we ran a pilot earlier this year — best practice: quarterly reconciliation and a 60–90 day payout lag to allow for churn checks. that reduced disputes.

[00:12:08] [00:12:08] Samir Patel: ok, process Q: for leads that Bluehaven qualifies and hands off, what's the acceptance SLA?
[00:12:16] Maya Chen: acceptance SLA is 48 hours for initial triage and 5 business days for technical validation. if not met, the lead returns to Bluehaven owner.

[00:12:30] Talia Morgan: reps want visibility in Salesforce. can we have a joint field on opportunity that shows partner status?
[00:12:38] Priya Rao: we support a field mapping doc. Maya will share the CSV mapping and Redwood ops will sync weekly to avoid data drift.

[00:12:50] Luca Fernandez: technical scoping note: for accounts with long context we should capture token distribution and expected concurrency; otherwise our cost model could be off by 30%.

[00:13:05] Ben Ortiz: would you be open to running a benchmark with Helix Investments' anonymized traces?
[00:13:12] Maya Chen: yes — if they can share anonymized request traces, our SE bench team can run a delta analysis. that's usually a 1–2 week turn.

[00:13:35] [00:13:35] Samir Patel: moving to enablement timeline — can we get the one-pager and sandbox access this week? reps need it for next Monday's field huddle.
[00:13:45] Maya Chen: we can ship the one-pager and sandbox invite by 2025-11-20. Luca will own the sandbox provisioning.

[00:14:02] Priya Rao: also thinking about a monthly co-sell standup. cadence: 30 minutes to review pipeline, highlight blockers, and escalate any security/legal items. good?
[00:14:12] Talia Morgan: yes, that helps keep momentum.

[00:14:20] Maya Chen: okay — recap of commitments: playbook + incentive sheet (Maya), sandbox + cost one-pager (Luca), account mapping from Bluehaven (Samir). we'll also schedule a 90-min deal-storm for top 4 accounts.

[00:14:42] [00:14:42] Ben Ortiz: one last technical ask — is there an example of a minimal on-prem POC SOW you can share?
[00:14:49] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include the minimal POC SOW in the security pack.

[00:15:05] [crosstalk — inaudible]
[00:15:12] Samir Patel: thanks all — very useful. can we confirm the executive intro timeline?
[00:15:18] Maya Chen: propose week of Nov 24; Priya and I will coordinate schedules.

[00:15:26] Talia Morgan: perfect. thanks everyone.
[00:15:29] Maya Chen: thanks — we'll follow up with links and the action items.

[00:15:35] [end of recorded transcript excerpt — call continued with deal-level micro-triage and calendar scheduling to 16:32]
